newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand hopeful of getting U.S. missiles.
newsitem.headline: Thailand hopeful of getting U.S. missiles.

text.p: Thailand's air force chief said on Thursday he was confident his country would get advanced, American-made air-to-air missiles despite the United States' recent refusal to sell them.
Thailand has been pressing Washington to sell it the AIM-120 Advanced Medium Range Air-to-Air missiles (AMRAAM) to equip the squadron of F/A-18 "Hornet" fighters it is buying from McDonnell Douglas.

Last month, a Thai Air Force delegation visited Washington with a fresh request for the missile, the most advanced of its kind. But U.S. officials turned it down for fear of sparking a Southeast Asian arms race, U.S. and Thai official sources said.
One said another reason for U.S. reluctance may be fears that the missile technology could leak to China.
"We will definitely get the missiles when we need them. That is part of the agreement that has been made," said Air Chief Marshal Siriphong Thongyai.

Although the deal for the missile purchase was not in the contract for the F-18 purchase, there was an agreement with the United States for the sale in a side letter to the contract, Siriphong said. He gave no further details.
The F-18 fighter sale, valued at US$578 million, was held up by initial Thai insistence that the missiles be included as part of a package deal.
As an alternative, Thailand had weighed buying competing French or Russian-built fighters equipped with AMRAAM-like active-radar-guided missiles.
